name: PCD Ops
description: The day-two dashboard. Resource reclamation and warnings, cluster capacity planning with what-if analysis and CPU and memory overcommit, a searchable inventory with host and VM metrics, snapshot management, right-sizing recommendations from real usage, anomaly detection, a config change log and alerts.
includes: Idle VMs, orphaned volumes, stale snapshots
AI triage with Claude or your own private AI

ports.purpose: Web UI over HTTP (redirects to HTTPS) and the health check

configuration.label: AI backend
configuration.help: Used for AI right-sizing, anomaly and log analysis. For Claude, enter the API key on the PCD Ops Settings page after install.

configuration.label: AI endpoint URL
configuration.help: Ollama base URL or OpenAI-compatible endpoint, reachable from the appliance. Settings lists its models after install.

configuration.label: AI model
configuration.help: Model name on the endpoint, e.g. llama3.1:8b.

post_deploy_notes: Open the URL over HTTPS and log in with your PCD account; you need the admin role in the project PCD Ops was installed into. The appliance makes a self-signed certificate at first boot, so the browser warns until you trust it or upload your own under Settings > HTTPS. The first admin to log in clicks Complete install (one click, no passwords). PCD Ops scrapes host and VM metrics itself (TCP 9388 and 9177 on the hypervisors); a Grafana service account token under Settings > Connection is optional and adds PCD's 14 days of history from the first day. If you use Claude, paste its API key under Settings > AI; AI settings from the install form are defaults that Settings can change. The appliance has no sshd; manage it from the VM console menu.
